claim.quote: The small Q^2 of this experiment has made possible the first determination of the weak charge of the proton

key_value.note: Q_W^p(PVES) from the commissioning run, as quoted in the abstract.
key_value.quote: The value of QpW obtained in this way is QpW(PVES) = 0.064 +- 0.012, in good agreement with the Standard Model prediction of QpW(SM) = 0.0710 +- 0.0007.

name: Qweak: first determination of the weak charge of the proton

summary.plain: Qweak's first result, from about 4% of its data: the smallest and most precise electron-proton asymmetry ever measured, which allowed the first determination of the proton's weak charge (0.064 ± 0.012, in agreement with the Standard Model).
summary.technical: Commissioning-run result: A_ep = -279 ± 35 (stat) ± 31 (syst) ppb at Q^2 = 0.025 (GeV/c)^2; with earlier PVES data constraining hadronic corrections, Q_W^p(PVES) = 0.064 ± 0.012 versus the Standard-Model 0.0710 ± 0.0007; combined with atomic parity violation, constraints on the up- and down-quark weak charges.

title: First Determination of the Weak Charge of the Proton
why_it_matters: First determination of the proton's weak charge, demonstrating the method that the full data set later sharpened.
